Workflow Setup and Execution

Workflow.Rmd

Typical Package Workflow

This vignette explains how to set up and run a reporting workflow with ospsuite.reportingframework.

Accessing the Workflow Template

To access the default workflow template provided by the package, you can use the following function:

openWorkflowTemplate()

This function opens the workflow template as a new document in your RStudio environment, allowing you to customize it for your specific needs. For detailed information on what each function in the workflow does, please refer to the help functionality in R.

Access via RStudio Addins

You can also access the workflow template through an RStudio Addin. To use the Addins, simply navigate to the Addins menu in RStudio and select “Open Template Workflow.” This will execute the openWorkflowTemplate() function and open the template in a new document.

AI-Assisted Workflow Setup

If you use an AI assistant to create or refine workflow scripts, you can generate project-specific prompts directly from the package.

prompt <- createAIPromptFromTask(
  projectConfiguration = projectConfiguration,
  task = "create-workflow"
)

cat(prompt, sep = "\n")

Available task presets are:

  • "create-workflow"
  • "import-data"
  • "build-plots"
  • "debug-run"

You can also export compact context data for other AI tools:

exportWorkflowContext(
  projectConfiguration = projectConfiguration,
  file = "workflow-context.json"
)

Before running AI-generated code, validate the configuration:

validation <- validateWorkflowForAI(projectConfiguration)
validation$ok
validation$errors

Customizing the Workflow Template

By default, the workflow template is loaded from the package’s internal templates. If you wish to customize this template, follow these steps:

  1. Create your own workflow template script and save it with the name template_workflow.R.
  2. Place this file in your designated template directory.
  3. Set the path to your custom template by using the following option:
options(OSPSuite.RF.PathForWorkflowTemplate = "myTemplateDirectory")

After setting this option, calling openWorkflowTemplate() or using the Addins will open your customized template instead of the default one. You can save this option in your “.Rprofile” file (file.path(Sys.getenv("HOME"), ".Rprofile")) to set it automatically.

Project Initialization

The first step in the workflow is to initialize the project. This includes:

  • Loading necessary libraries.
  • Setting the workflow options.
  • Setting up the project directory and configuration files by initializing with esqlabsR and upgrading to ReportingFramework defaults (unless keepEsqlabsRStructure = TRUE).
  • Creating or updating .gitignore files in configuration folders so *.xlsx configuration files are ignored by Git.
  • Initializing the log file.

Set workflow behavior with setWorkflowOptions(isValidRun). This controls whether exploratory outputs are allowed (isValidRun = FALSE) or a QC-passed run is enforced (isValidRun = TRUE). If isValidRun is omitted, getQCpassedEnvironmentVariable() reads QCpassed from the environment.

# Exploratory run: enable watermarks and allow helper functions
setWorkflowOptions(isValidRun = FALSE)

# QC-passed run: disable watermarks and enforce strict execution
setWorkflowOptions(isValidRun = TRUE)

Initialize the project structure. By default, analysisSubfolderName = "ReportingFramework" creates Scripts/ReportingFramework and Outputs/ReportingFramework. Set a custom name if you want multiple analyses that share the same project-level models and data folders.

analysisSubfolderName <- "RF_Analysis"
initProject(
  projectDirectory = ".",
  analysisSubfolderName = analysisSubfolderName,
  keepEsqlabsRStructure = FALSE
)

configurationDirectory <- file.path("Scripts", analysisSubfolderName)

Create and load the project configuration from the project workbook path:

projectConfiguration <- createProjectConfiguration(
  path = file.path(configurationDirectory, "ProjectConfiguration.xlsx"),
  ignoreVersionCheck = FALSE
)

ProjectConfiguration.xlsx stores the package versions used to create the project: esqlabsRVersion (managed by esqlabsR) and ospsuiteReportingFrameworkVersion (managed by this package). When you load a configuration, both versions are checked against installed packages; mismatches prompt for update in interactive sessions and stop execution in non-interactive runs (for example CI) until resolved. New projects created with initProject() receive the current framework version automatically, and projectConfiguration$save() updates stored version values.

Ownership and Side Effects Matrix

The reporting workflow combines base esqlabsR configuration with reporting add-ons. The table below summarizes ownership and whether common functions read or modify each workbook.

Workbook / Sheet Primary owner Typical usage in workflows Modified by reporting framework functions
ProjectConfiguration.xlsx esqlabsR base + RF extension fields Loaded by createProjectConfiguration() ProjectConfigurationRF$save() updates stored paths/versions
ProjectConfiguration.xlsx (AddOns) Reporting framework extension layer Stores add-on workbook/folder references such as dataImportMapFile, reportsFile, pKParameterFile, and electronicPackageFolder Initialized/updated by upgradeToReportingFramework() and persisted by ProjectConfigurationRF$save()
Scenarios.xlsx (Scenarios, OutputPaths) esqlabsR Read by simulation workflow and synchronization helpers Usually not modified by readObservedDataByDictionary(). It may be read to synchronize plot-facing sheets.
Individuals.xlsx (IndividualBiometrics) esqlabsR workbook, populated by RF import helpers Used for individual metadata and population-related workflows addBiometricsToConfig() appends/updates observed biometrics
Individuals.xlsx (VirtualTwinPopulation) Reporting framework add-on sheet Used by virtual twin population workflows setupVirtualTwinPopConfig() creates/updates this sheet
DataImportMap.xlsx Reporting framework add-on workbook Read by readObservedDataByDictionary() as import dictionary Not modified by import execution
Reports.xlsx (DataGroups, Outputs, Scenarios) Reporting framework add-on workbook Read by runPlot() and report generation updateDataGroupId() updates DataGroups; updateOutputPathId() updates Outputs; scenario rows can be synchronized into Scenarios
PKParameter.xlsx Reporting framework add-on workbook Used for PK parameter selection and user-defined PK settings Modified only when users edit configuration manually

For data import, side effects are controlled by spreadData in readObservedDataByDictionary(). Set spreadData = FALSE for read-only imports (returns imported data without propagating identifiers/metadata into configuration workbooks).

Logging and Diagnostics

Set up logging immediately after loading the project configuration so workflow messages, warnings, and errors are written to a predictable location.

setLogPath(
  logFolder = file.path(projectConfiguration$outputFolder, "logs"),
  logFileName = "workflow.log"
)

This creates a log file in projectConfiguration$outputFolder/logs. Use this log as the primary record for workflow execution in local runs and CI.

Wrap workflow steps with captureLog() when you want messages, warnings, and errors from a code block to be routed to the log file while still propagating errors to the caller:

captureLog({
  importedData <- readObservedDataFromDataSet(
    projectConfiguration = projectConfiguration,
    dataFile = "observed-data.csv"
  )
})

Use addMessageToLog() for progress markers or decisions that should appear in the log, and writeTableToLog() when a data frame snapshot helps with debugging:

addMessageToLog("Observed data import finished")
writeTableToLog(head(importedData$data))

If console output becomes too noisy during interactive work, hide informational messages while still keeping warnings in the console:

setShowLogMessages(FALSE)

For reproducibility or support requests, save the current R session details next to the workflow log:

saveSessionInfo()

This writes sessionInfo.log into the configured log folder and is useful when investigating package version or environment-specific issues.

Configuration in Git: Use JSON Snapshots

Configuration workbooks (*.xlsx) are generated working files and are ignored by Git in configuration folders. The versioned source of truth is the JSON snapshot created from the configuration.

Save current configuration to JSON:

projectConfiguration <- createProjectConfiguration(
  path = file.path(configurationDirectory, "ProjectConfiguration.xlsx")
)

snapshotProjectConfigurationRF(
  projectConfiguration,
  outputDir = configurationDirectory
)

This writes ProjectConfiguration.json in configurationDirectory. Commit this JSON file to Git.

Restore configuration from JSON (for example on another machine or in CI):

projectConfiguration <- restoreProjectConfigurationRF(
  snapshotFilePath = file.path(configurationDirectory, "ProjectConfiguration.json"),
  outputDir = configurationDirectory
)

Data Import

After initialization, the first step should always be data import. The input format for data is CSV files, which can be imported using a dictionary. The imported data types include individual and aggregated time profile data as well as individual and aggregated PK parameter data.

For more information, see Data Import by Dictionary.

Setting Up and Running Simulations Including PK Parameter Calculation

Simulations are set up and run using the esqlabsR package. For more information and detailed documentation, users can visit the esqlabsR Documentation.

The ospsuite.reportingframework package provides additional functionality to:

  • Export random and virtual twin populations (see the Population).
  • Calculate PK Parameters (see the PK Parameters).

Plot and Report Generation

The core functionality of this package lies in plot and report creation. It includes various plotting functions that generate visualizations based on the analyses performed.

Each plot function is designed to create an R Markdown (.Rmd) file, which contains the code and output for the respective plot. This allows for easy documentation and sharing of results.

The package provides a collection of plot functions and interfaces to adjust plots and utilize customized plot functions.

For more information, see the Plot and Report Generation.
